### 1. 2026-11-03 23:50 UTC

> What is the command to run Langfuse sync? Create a script similar to run-verification that waits for new sync tasks and executes them in a background process.

**Reply:**

The Langfuse sync command is `python3 llm-dlc/tools/sync.py langfuse`, and I added a loop script that runs it whenever new work appears. I committed it, and `sync.py check` reports 0 errors.

**The command**
- `sync.py langfuse SID[:live]...` sends the finished turns of the sessions you name to Langfuse. It was already there.
- Normally the Stop hook sends each turn as it ends. The command is for sessions whose hook ran while Langfuse was down.
- I added `sync.py langfuse --pending`, which lists sessions with turns not yet sent. I added `sync.py langfuse --all` to send them. A mark in each session's state file records which stored log has been checked, so polling is cheap.
- A session still running keeps its last turn for the Stop hook. If Langfuse isn't configured, nothing is sent or marked as done.

**The loop script**
- `llm-dlc/tools/langfuse-loop.sh` is modelled on `verification-loop.sh`. Every `LANGFUSE_LOOP_POLL` seconds (default 30) it lists pending sessions and runs `--all` when there are any.
- If Langfuse is down, it logs the failure once and retries on the next poll.
- No Claude session is involved, since sending is mechanical.
- While it runs, you can type `stop`, `now`, or `?` (lists the pending sessions).

To run it in the background: `llm-dlc/tools/langfuse-loop.sh &`.

**Testing**
I tested it against your local Langfuse. It sent the 19 pending sessions, then idled on "nothing to send".
